Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

action noun

something done; doing

also deed, act, take action, actions

classical

Caesar in Cic. Att. 9.16.2: meum factum probārī abs tē
Hor. Ep. 1.2.40: dīmidium factī

factum, factī n.

noun, second declension

deed, act, what someone has done

Latin often says what was done with a verb or a relative clause: quod fēcistī, what you did.

Examples

  • virtūtis enim laus omnis in āctiōne cōnsistit

    for all the praise of virtue lies in actionCic. Off. 1.19

  • atque ego cum ex ipsā rē magnam capiō voluptātem tum meum factum probārī abs tē triumphō gaudiō

    and while I take great pleasure in the thing itself, I am overjoyed that you approve of my actionCaesar in Cic. Att. 9.16.2

  • dīmidium factī, quī coepit, habet; sapere audē, incipe

    well begun is half done: dare to be wise, make a startHor. Ep. 1.2.40–41

Other words

  • āctiō, āctiōnis f. — doing, action (as against thought or rest)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.19: virtūtis enim laus omnis in āctiōne cōnsistit

    Action in general rather than a single deed; in law, a lawsuit (see activity).

  • agō, agere, ēgī, āctum — act, do, take action

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 17: gubernātōrem in nāvigandō nihil agere

    “Take action” is agere or rem agere; nihil agere, to do nothing.

See also activity, event, make.
